_models: Current model ids per provider are documented in Models.md.
_modelProvider: OpenCode addresses a model as provider/model (e.g. openrouter/qwen/qwen3-vl-235b-a22b-instruct). Set modelProvider (e.g. "openrouter") next to a bare model instead of writing that prefix yourself.
_bin: providers.<name>.bin is a command name looked up on PATH, or a path (absolute, ~, or project-relative) that overrides PATH and pins a specific install.

codex._codex: model is the default used when a task names none. models is an allowlist: a task file's model:/variant: front matter may only pick from it; an unknown model or a variant its model does not list is ignored in favour of the default.

_modelTiers: Ordered capability registry, spanning providers. Higher `tier` = more capable; models sharing a tier are ranked by array order (earlier = higher priority). The harness uses it to refuse to switch a task to a less capable model during escalation/fallback. Every model the harness may run should have an entry; fill in your own ids. `model_tier`/`modelTier` are accepted aliases for `tier`.
_modelTierPolicy: What to do when a configured escalation/fallback target is a lower tier than the model running the task: downgrade (switch anyway), wait (keep retrying the current model with backoff), or block (stop the run for a human).

escalation._escalation: When a task fails (or a review reports `rework`), hand it to this provider/model. `variant` sets the reasoning effort for escalated sessions only; unset inherits the escalation provider's default. A task may override any of these with `escalation*` front matter, which wins.

fallback._fallback: When the primary provider keeps dying on a transient infrastructure fault (dropped connection, 5xx, model not available, resource busy), switch the task to this provider/model after `afterAttempts` exponential retries. Unlike escalation this reacts to infrastructure faults, not task failures. Example: a second OpenCode routed through a MorphLLM provider. Listing a normally-fatal category such as "model" also routes a model-unavailable failure here instead of halting.

flex._flex: When a flex service-tier variant (a variant named with `variantPrefix`, default `flex-`, or listed in `variants`) loses upstream capacity, a capacity fault is a routing event, not a task failure. `onUnavailable` decides: `wait` (default) polls every `pollSec` until flex frees up and then runs — bounded only by `maxWaitMin` (0 = indefinitely) so an unattended run rides out a capacity dip — `block` parks the task and halts for a human, and `fallback` switches to the configured `fallback` provider/model immediately. A wait never spends the retry, attempts or iteration budgets. `onCategories` names the failure categories treated as capacity faults; a normally-fatal `model`/`config` failure whose message names the flex pool/endpoints also counts.

vision.prompt: Describe this image accurately for someone who cannot see it. If a specific question or focus follows, answer that first and include the visual evidence that supports it. Otherwise, describe the salient subjects, setting, visible actions, and spatial relationships; for screenshots, documents, charts, or diagrams, include important controls, labels, values, text, and connections as relevant. Quote only legible text, note uncertain or obscured details, and distinguish what is visible from inference. Do not claim identity, location, or behavior that the image does not establish.

slack._slack: Target a channel and/or a user: slack.channel is a channel id (C…/G…/D…) or #name; slack.user is a user id (U…/W…) or @handle. Set one, or both with mention:true to ping the user in the channel.

judge._judge: Off by default. When enabled, after a task reports done and its verify passes, a separate read-only session reviews the task's Goal/Scope/acceptance against the worktree diff and returns pass/fail. onFail fail demotes a confident rejection so retry/escalation/breakdown re-engage; warn is advisory. Add "judge" to escalation.onCategories and breakdown.rules.onCategories to have those react to a rejected done.

mcp._mcp: Off by default: the harness never touches a client's MCP config. With enabled:true each session gets only its selection — task front matter "mcp:"/"capabilities:" wins, then mcp.sessions.<kind>, then mcp.defaultServers; --mcp/--no-mcp override a run. A server needs a command (stdio) or url (remote) for claude/codex/opencode to enable or disable it inline; a name-only entry still works for Gemini's allowlist.

progress._progress: On by default. After each attempt the harness fingerprints HEAD, non-harness worktree changes, acceptance checkboxes, the gate board and the verify result. A task that reports continue while reproducing a prior attempt's fingerprint has made no net progress: it is classified stalled, re-scoped or parked as a scope question instead of retried. Only an exact repeat can fire, so genuine work is never flagged.

metric._metric: Optional objective product signal. Set command to a shell command that prints a number (the metric is its last number). The harness samples it per attempt and parks a task whose metric has plateaued, so retry/split/accept follow an externally observable signal rather than the agent's narrative. direction: increase|decrease|nonzero.

ceiling._ceiling: Hard autonomy bounds. maxCostUsdPerTask / maxMinutesPerTask park a task (blocked) instead of retrying once reached; maxSplitDepth bounds a split chain. 0 disables a bound.
